As well as human resources, anchorages, channels, lighters, tugs, berths, warehouse, and other storage spaces have to be allocated and released. The efficient management of a port involves managing these various activities and resources to ensure smooth operations, maintain safety, and minimize environmental impact. One of the primary aspects of port management is the planning and execution of port activities. This involves coordinating the allocation of resources, such as berths, anchorages, and storage spaces, to ensure that ships and cargo can be efficiently and effectively managed. This includes the scheduling of ships' arrivals and departures, as well as the allocation of equipment and personnel to handle cargo and other port activities. Another critical aspect of port management is the oversight of port operations. This includes the management of human resources, the maintenance of port infrastructure, and the monitoring of port activities to ensure that they are conducted safely and in compliance with regulatory requirements. Effective port management also involves the maintenance of strong relationships with port users, such as shipping lines, cargo owners, and other stakeholders, to ensure that the port's services are meeting their needs. In recent years, the role of technology in port management has become increasingly important. Ports are increasingly adopting advanced technologies, such as automation, information systems, and advanced analytics, to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of their operations. Geologically, it forms an eroded anticline along the Bray fault, a fold in the Earth’s crust on the edge of the Parisian Basin. This structure has exposed sedimentary layers, contrasting with the surrounding chalk plateaus. The clay underpinnings, combined with the region’s low-lying, water-retentive terrain, historically shaped its pastoral economy and contributed to its reputation for dairy products. It is a smaller version of the Weald of Kent and Sussex, but reveals the beds more deeply; down to the Upper Jurassic clay.
